title: Gujarat's Swaminarayan
hook: a whole community names itself after the company it keeps

segments.voice: Yesterday, Gujarat's Swaminarayan: the Shikshapatri, a short letter meant to be read every day. Which line of good counsel did you come back to? Day one thousand four hundred four.

Ask a Swaminarayan devotee what they belong to, and you may hear a word you weren't expecting. Not a membership, not a congregation. Satsang. A devotee is a satsangi. The weekly gathering is a satsang sabha. The whole fellowship, across Gujarat and in cities far from it, is spoken of as the satsang. It's an old Sanskrit word, used across Hindu traditions, and some families use it for a Sunday evening of singing in someone's living room. But here it's become a name for a whole community. Today, a word that names people by the company they keep.
screen: `NOT A MEMBERSHIP.` → `SATSANGI, SATSANG SABHA.` → `NAMED BY THE COMPANY KEPT.`

segments.voice: The word comes apart into two pieces. Sat is what is true, what is real, what is good. Sang is company, association, being together. So satsang is the company of the true, or the company of the good. It has three layers. The first is the company of good people. In the Vachanamrut, Swaminarayan speaks about the company a seeker keeps, and how it shapes them. The idea is plain enough to recognize from ordinary life. Spend your evenings with people who gossip, and gossip gets easier. Spend them with people who are patient, and patience starts to rub off. Satsang treats that as a spiritual fact, not just a social one. The second layer is the company of the holy. In the Swaminarayan tradition, satsang especially means time near God and near a true sadhu, a holy person, someone whose life shows the teaching. Being near such a person, listening, serving, watching how they handle an insult or a hard day, is itself a practice. The third is the company of good words. Satsang also happens when people gather to hear scripture read and explained, the Vachanamrut, the Shikshapatri, the songs of the tradition's poet-sadhus. Words become company too. So when a community calls itself the satsang, it's making a kind of promise. We are the people who try to keep good company, and who try to be good company for each other. That's a lot to put in one word. It's also a test anyone can run on an ordinary week.
screen: `SAT — TRUE; SANG — COMPANY` · `GOOD PEOPLE RUB OFF` · `NEAR GOD AND A TRUE SADHU` · `GOOD WORDS AS COMPANY`

segments.voice: Sit, and let the breath slow, and take stock of your company. Bring to mind one person whose company leaves you a little better than before: calmer, kinder, more honest. Picture their face for a moment. Notice what it is about them. Then bring to mind someone who might say the same about you. Let both of them sit with you for a few breaths, without any judgment. If you pray, you can hold them both before God. The bell holds the time.
Gujarat's Swaminarayan. Today, satsang, the company of the true, the name the Swaminarayan community uses for itself. Today's word.
Your line: Gujarat's Swaminarayan. Today, spend ten unhurried minutes with the person you pictured, or send them a message saying what their company does for you. Day one thousand four hundred four.

howItsDone: Swaminarayan devotees gather in weekly satsang assemblies at mandirs and in homes, with singing, readings from the scriptures and talks by sadhus or senior devotees.

notes: Confirm that Swaminarayan devotees commonly refer to the whole fellowship as 'the satsang', to a follower as a 'satsangi', and to the weekly gathering as a 'satsang sabha'.

The teach says the Vachanamrut speaks 'often' about the company a seeker keeps and about association with a true sadhu (sant/satpurush). Paraphrase only; a Keeper may wish to cite specific discourses.

Different Swaminarayan organizations understand the 'true sadhu' differently (e.g. the guru lineage in BAPS, the acharyas and sadhus in the Ahmedabad and Vadtal dioceses); the script stays general on purpose.
Etymology of satsang (sat + sanga) is standard Sanskrit; confirm pronunciation 'SUT-sung'.
Index word and carry are the part title; written to it as required.
